chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Indeed, the believer is known in the heavens just as a man knows his family and children, and he is more honored before Allah than a nearby-stationed angel.

key_terms.مَلَك مُقَرَّب: Nearby-stationed angel (specifically referring to angels close to God's throne or presence)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a believer in the heavens according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition to illustrate the unique ontological elevation of the believer, whose identity is so distinct in the heavens that they are recognized with the same intimacy as a father knows his children. This comparison underscores the believer's superior status over the *Muqarrabun* (closely attendant angels), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the human capacity to embody divine attributes and achieve a rank that even the highest angels do not possess.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-62 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
Indeed a believer is known in the heavens just as a man knows his wife and children. He is more honored before God than the nearby-stationed angel.”
